rules.comment: Workaround for a Colemak bug in the Claude app: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/68859. Note: the macOS Colemak input source re-translates Karabiner's output, so to send the app Cmd+K we emit key_code n (Colemak maps the n-position to 'k'). Digits are not remapped by Colemak, so Cmd+3 is emitted as-is.
rules.description: Claude app: Cmd+J -> Cmd+K, Cmd+3

rules.comment: Clicks the project selector on the New Conversation screen. Claude's Electron renderer exposes no accessibility tree, so the button cannot be targeted by name and the position is hardcoded. Coordinates are absolute on the main display, so this only lands correctly while the Claude window sits in its usual position and size. restore-mouse-position.js saves the cursor position and puts it back afterward, since Karabiner can move the cursor but cannot read it; the 200ms hold gives it time to read the position before the cursor moves, and the 100ms hold keeps the click from racing the cursor move.
rules.description: Claude app: Cmd+P -> click project selector (physical key r in Colemak)

rules.comment: Clicks the Create PR button in the session view. Like the Cmd+P project-selector rule, the Electron renderer exposes no accessibility tree, so the position is hardcoded. Coordinates are absolute on the main display; y matches the project-selector rule, x is the button's position in a 2x Retina screenshot (1313 px) halved to points. restore-mouse-position.js saves the cursor position and puts it back afterward, since Karabiner can move the cursor but cannot read it; the 200ms hold gives it time to read the position before the cursor moves. The 100ms hold is needed because without it the click races the cursor move and the app registers only the hover, so the shortcut had to be pressed twice.
rules.description: Claude app: Cmd+Shift+P -> click Create PR button (physical key r in Colemak)

rules.comment: Show Diff. The app ignores Cmd+Shift+D while the chat box has focus, so the rule first clicks an empty spot in the sidebar to blur it. Like the Cmd+P and Cmd+Shift+P rules, the coordinates are absolute on the main display and only land correctly while the Claude window sits in its usual position and size. restore-mouse-position.js saves the cursor position and puts it back afterward, since Karabiner can move the cursor but cannot read it; the 200ms hold gives it time to read the position before the cursor moves, since Karabiner runs shell_command asynchronously and would otherwise move the cursor first and leave the script saving (230, 940). Script startup measured 70-110ms over five runs, so 200ms is roughly twice the slowest; raise it if the cursor ever ends up parked in the sidebar. The two 100ms holds keep the click from racing the cursor move and give the app time to move focus before the keystroke arrives.
rules.description: Claude app: Cmd+Shift+G -> click empty sidebar (230, 940), Cmd+Shift+D

rules.comment: Archives the current session via the command palette. This replaces the earlier Cmd+Shift+E -> Cmd+Shift+E rule that reached the app's effort picker; the effort picker now stays on its default position (physical e, the key that types 'f' in Colemak). Cmd+K is emitted as key_code n for the same Colemak re-translation bug as the Cmd+J rule (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/68859). The letters after it are ordinary text typed into the palette's search field, and text input always goes through the macOS Colemak input source, so each letter is emitted as the physical key that types it: 'archive' = a s c h l v k, with a, c, h, and v unchanged by Colemak. Enter is not remapped by Colemak. The pauses are conservative first guesses, not tuned: 150ms after Cmd+K for the palette to open and focus its search field, and 120ms before Enter so it does not run whatever is selected before the filter catches up to 'archive'; raise them if letters drop or the wrong command runs. Cmd+1 afterwards navigates to the first chat, with 150ms after Enter for the archive to complete and the palette to close first, so the shortcut lands on the chat list rather than the closing palette. Digits are not remapped by Colemak, so 1 is emitted as-is. The trailing vk_none keeps Cmd+1 from being the last event, since Karabiner holds the last event down until the from key is released and a held key would repeat into whatever has focus.
rules.description: Claude app: Cmd+Shift+E -> Cmd+K, type 'archive', Enter, Cmd+1 (physical key k in Colemak)

rules.comment: Clicks the Always apply link in the toast that Shortwave shows in the bottom-right corner after a label is applied, which promotes that one-off into a standing rule. The toast offers no keyboard shortcut, so the mouse is the only route. The link is visible for as long as the toast is up rather than only on hover, so a plain warp and click lands on it and the slower mouse-click.js walk is not needed. restore-mouse-position.js saves the cursor position and puts it back afterward, since Karabiner can move the cursor but cannot read it; the 200ms hold gives it time to read the position before the cursor moves, and the 100ms hold keeps the click from racing the cursor move. The click clears its modifiers because the physical Option is still down when it is posted, and the trailing vk_none keeps the button press from being the last to event, which would hold the mouse button down until Option+A is released and drag instead of click. Coordinates are absolute on the main display and only land correctly while the Shortwave window sits in its usual position and size and the toast is showing.
rules.description: Shortwave: Option+A -> click Always apply on the label toast (1272, 890)

rules.comment: Archives the top notification in the Inbox side panel by handing the whole gesture to a script, which moves the pointer there with real mouse events and clicks. Karabiner's own set_mouse_cursor_position warps the cursor without posting a mouse-moved event, and that is the root of every problem this rule has had: Chromium does not update its hover target from a warp, so the archive button, which only exists while the row is hovered, is either not armed or no longer armed when the click lands, and the click hit-tests against the row underneath and opens the notification instead. Waiting it out does not work reliably, because the window is bounded at both ends. Measured from the warp, with a single click: 60-80ms is too early and hits the row, 130ms archives, 250ms archives with false negatives, 400-500ms fails outright, and 150ms managed 1 in 4, so the window is narrow, drifts, and is not worth aiming at. An earlier two-click version appeared to work by firing at two offsets and landing one inside the window, which also means it archives twice whenever both land. The script sidesteps the window by walking the pointer in steps with CGEvents, which Chromium treats as genuine motion. Posting CGEvents needs Accessibility permission, which osascript does not have on its own, but Karabiner does and the processes it spawns inherit it; run the same command from a terminal and the events are silently filtered and the pointer never moves. It also clears the modifier flags on the click, since the physical Cmd+Shift are still down and an uncleared click arrives as Shift+Click and extends the text selection across the page, and it restores the cursor itself. Notion has no keyboard shortcut for archiving a single notification, so the mouse is the only route. Coordinates are absolute on the main display and only land correctly while the Notion window is top-left aligned at its usual size with the Inbox panel open; y is measured from the top of the first row rather than its middle, so it holds regardless of how tall the notification is, and the three buttons sit about 10 points apart, so shift x by 10 if the click lands on a neighbor.
rules.description: Notion: Cmd+Shift+E -> click archive on top notification (166, 135) (physical key k in Colemak)

rules.comment: Opens the emoji picker for the last received message, so any emoji can be sent as a tapback without touching the mouse. The hover tapback bar is anchored to the message bubble, so it moves with the message's width and height and no fixed coordinate can reach its picker. The right-click menu is anchored to the click point instead, so the rule right-clicks a fixed point on the last message and works from there. (360, 890) sits inside the last received bubble whatever its size: received bubbles are left aligned at x 348 so a short message still covers x 360, and the transcript is bottom anchored so the bubble's lower edge stays at y 900 however tall the message is. A sent message is right aligned and will not be hit. move-to-tapback-picker.js then reads the menu's own window frame rather than assuming where it landed, because macOS pins the menu above the bottom of the screen and the height it pins from changes with the menu's items, so a message carrying a link would otherwise be off by the height of the extra ones; if no menu appears it leaves the pointer alone and the click lands back on the message. The right-click is held for 150ms rather than clicked instantly, which is what makes it reliable: the menu opens on the mouse down and starts a modal tracking loop, and an immediate mouse up can arrive before that loop is installed and dismiss it, which failed 5 times in 6 before the hold and 0 times in 6 after. Karabiner posts both clicks itself because it holds Accessibility and the osascript it spawns does not, which is also why the script only warps the pointer. The 200ms hold lets restore-mouse-position.js read the pointer before it moves, the 100ms hold keeps the right-click from racing the cursor move, and the 550ms hold covers osascript startup, measured at 70-110ms, plus the script's 250ms poll for the menu. Coordinates are absolute on the main display and only land correctly while the Messages window sits in its usual position and size with the conversation scrolled to the bottom; a group conversation indents received bubbles past x 360.
rules.description: Messages: Cmd+E -> open the emoji picker for the last received message (physical key k in Colemak)
